messages:
Sam (product): Heads-up: we need to decide sequencing for the next release — customers pushing both API ergonomics (SDK helpers, better error surface) and console admin features (RBAC, route dashboards). Can we run quick RICE-ish tradeoff and pick a phasing?
Maya (eng): +1. Engineering capacity is limited this quarter. Console pieces touch frontend, auth, and runtime wiring. API & SDK work is more contained.
Jon (devex): From a new-user onboarding POV, API examples + SDKs reduce 50% of support tickets. Console admin helps enterprise buyers in sales cycles.
Priya (sales): To be blunt: two EEs asked for RBAC + audit logs yesterday. They won't sign without admin surface. But 5 smaller startups asked for a nicer SDK first.
Carlos (cto): We should define objective criteria: launch-readiness must include perf SLOs, telemetry hooks, and docs. Also consider long-term maintenance cost — console UI has higher ongoing support.
Sam (product): Proposed framing: prioritize by near-term revenue vs. expansion velocity. Quick RICE sketch for two epics (API+SDK vs Console admin):
Sam (product): - API+SDK: Reach=7, Impact=6, Confidence=0.7, Effort=6 (team-weeks) -> RICE ~= (7*6*0.7)/6 = 4.9
Sam (product): - Console admin: Reach=4, Impact=8, Confidence=0.6, Effort=12 -> RICE ~= (4*8*0.6)/12 = 1.6
Maya (eng): Numbers feel reasonable. Effort for console could balloon (integration with RBAC, KMS, audit pipeline). Also needs E2E tests across Dedicated/Private variants.
Jon (devex): Can we slice console into a smaller "admin read-only" surface first? That would let sales demo without full manage flows. Low dev effort, medium impact.
Priya (sales): Read-only consoles are fine for sales demos, but some legal/compliance customers need active RBAC + SSO before procurement. We can accept a two-track approach: close deals where possible with read-only, but prioritize RBAC for top-3 target accounts.
Carlos (cto): Two-track sounds sensible. Also require canary rollout + usage metrics for any new console feature. If console causes regressions we must have automatic fallback to API-only flows.
Sam (product): New proposal (phased):
Sam (product): Phase A (4w): API ergonomics + SDK helpers, improved error payloads, small docs refresh. Goal: reduce onboarding tickets and quick wins for PLG.
Sam (product): Phase B (3w): "Admin read-only" console slice: account-level dashboards, activity logs (view-only), and demo-mode toggles. Low-risk; supports demos.
Sam (product): Phase C (6-10w, sales-driven): RBAC + audit logs + SSO for top customers behind a gated rollout. Prioritize implementation for Dedicated/Private earlier.
Maya (eng): Rough implementation estimates: Phase A = 5 eng-weeks (API core + SDK + tests), Phase B = 4 eng-weeks (frontend + telemetry), Phase C = 12 eng-weeks (auth infra + QA across deployments).
Jon (devex): For Phase A I can spin up quick sample apps and a migration guide in 1 week. That will amplify reach.
Priya (sales): I'll map the top 6 opportunities and mark which need RBAC vs read-only demos. We'll push legal-prep for the top-3 that require RBAC.
Carlos (cto): Add launch criteria per phase: no P0 bugs in the first 72h, observability for request-level tracing, rollbacks via flags, and KB articles for common failures.
Sam (product): Agreed. Also adding success metrics: Phase A -> reduce onboarding tickets 30% in 30 days; Phase B -> demo conversion +10%; Phase C -> close 2 enterprise deals in Q after rollout.
Maya (eng): One risk: if we build SDKs for every language, effort explodes. Recommend prioritizing Python + Node first, then expand.
Jon (devex): +1 on language prioritization. We'll include code samples for Go + Java as lightweight snippets but not full SDKs initially.
Sam (product): Ok action items: 1) Maya to give final eng estimates by EOD Monday. 2) Jon to draft SDK rollout plan + sample apps. 3) Priya to share top-6 accounts and RBAC needs. 4) Carlos to confirm SSO/KMS constraints for Private.
deploy-bot: Scheduled canary flagged for Phase B on 1750006000.
Priya (sales)::+1: on the plan. If Phase A shows traction we can defer some console work into next quarter.
Maya (eng): Noted. Starting backlog tickets: API ergonomics epic, SDK epic, admin-readonly epic. We'll attach estimates.
Sam (product): Thanks all — I'll convert this thread into a short spec and RICE table, then we'll review in the Tuesday triage slot. :sparkles:
